title: Add PRD requirements: fallback exposure mitigation, synthetic burn-in, and SLO validation gates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Translate recent postmortem actions into discrete PRD requirements that reduce fallback exposure during partial service degradation and ensure releases include automated SLO validation and synthetic burn-in before traffic ramp. Goals: 1) Prevent excessive user-visible fallbacks by limiting fallback exposure windows and introducing passive safeguard modes; 2) Require a synthetic burn-in run for any rollout that changes routing, cache priming, or kernel selection behavior; 3) Add SLO validation gates (latency, error-rate, token-cost) to the release checklist and integrate automated canary checks that must pass before canary expansion. Scope: This PRD section covers product-level requirements and acceptance criteria for hosted and dedicated deployments; runtime implementation details will be driven by ENG tickets (see dependencies). Out of scope: full rework of kernel-selection heuristics (addressed separately).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Release checklist contains a 'Fallback Exposure Mitigation' section with three required items: max-fallback-duration (configurable default 60s), fallback-rate cap at edge (default 2% of requests), and post-fallback telemetry tagging for downstream analysis.

A2: Synthetic burn-in harness exists and can run a configurable workload for 30–120 minutes; it must exercise routing, cache priming, and quantized model variants. The PRD defines the burn-in profile and pass/fail thresholds.

A3: Canary must run SLO validation checks (p99 latency, request error-rate, token cost per inference) against baseline for at least two synthetic scenarios; automatic rollback triggers if any metric regresses beyond configured thresholds.

A4: Console shows a dedicated 'Fallback Exposure' dashboard with per-route rollout exposure, counts of fallback vs native responses, and a time-to-first-fallback metric. Dashboard widgets are included in the release artifact.

A5: Runbook appendix created with step-by-step actions for: identifying fallback storms, initiating emergency rollback, temporarily enabling passive safeguard mode, and contacting on-call owners. Runbook is linked in the PRD and validated by SRE during the rollout rehearsal.
A6: All new telemetry fields (fallback_reason, fallback_variant, canary_burnin_id) are documented and present in the event schema and exported to metrics/logs for at least 90 days by default.
A7: Product accepts a signed-off risk statement from Eng and SRE confirming feasibility and estimated cost delta for synthetic burn-in and canary validation (must be attached to PRD).
